name: Paediatric Urology, Hypospadias, Cryptorchidism, and Wilms Tumor

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Campbell-Walsh Urology 12th ed
clinicalPearls: Neonatal circumcision is strictly contraindicated in hypospadias; foreskin is required for reconstruction
Surgical orchidopexy between 6 and 12 months preserves germ cells and reduces malignant degeneration risk
Posterior urethral valves cause lower urinary tract obstruction in male neonates; keyhole sign on ultrasound
Wilms tumor presents as a smooth, firm flank mass that rarely crosses the midline in children aged 2-4 years
Biopsy of Wilms tumor is strictly contraindicated; management combines chemotherapy and radical nephrectomy
reference.pathophysiology: Hypospadias results from failure of the urethral folds to fuse ventrally over the urethral groove. Cryptorchidism involves mechanical or endocrine failure of gubernacular testicular descent. Wilms tumor arises from persistent metanephric blastema secondary to mutations in WT1 (11p13) or WTX, expanding into a triphasic neoplasm of blastemal, epithelial, and stromal cells.
additionalDifferentials: Neuroblastoma (calcified adrenal mass crossing aortic midline, elevated urinary catecholamines)
Polycystic kidney disease / multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK)
Testicular retractile reflex (normal variant, manual milking into scrotum succeeds)
additionalInvestigations: Voiding cystourethrography (VCUG) evaluating posterior urethral valves and vesicoureteral reflux
Diagnostic laparoscopy for impalpable undescended testicle
Abdominal and chest CT for staging and inferior vena cava patency in Wilms tumor
